overall: The AG found the Board violated the OML by repeatedly approving minutes late and failing to review executive session minutes at reasonable intervals for about five years; it ordered in-person training and future compliance, declining the other allegations.

allegations.summary: Board repeatedly approved open and executive session minutes late, in violation of the timely-approval requirement, over about five years.
allegations.key_passage: For these reasons, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by routinely failing to approve minutes of both open and executive sessions in a timely manner.

allegations.summary: Board failed to periodically review executive session minutes at reasonable intervals to decide whether they could be released.
allegations.key_passage: For these reasons, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to review its executive session minutes at reasonable intervals to determine whether continued nondisclosure was warranted or whether the minutes could be released to the public.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board omitted a public comment item from its December 14, 2018 and January 2, 2019 meetings.
allegations.key_passage: Even if true, these allegations would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged violations of G.L. c. 269A, §21A, a statute outside the AG's Open Meeting Law enforcement jurisdiction.
allegations.key_passage: The complaints also allege violations of G.L. c. 269A, §21 A, a statute which is not within the jurisdiction of our Division to enforce the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the April 3, 2017 meeting notice did not list an anticipated item; the allegation was untimely.
allegations.key_passage: However, this allegation is untimely as it could have been discovered at the time the open session took place.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the April 3, 2017 minutes lacked sufficient detail about a Warrant Article 25 discussion; the allegation was untimely.
allegations.key_passage: However, this allegation is also untimely because the alleged lack of detail could have been discovered when the minutes were approved on April 18, 2017.

allegations.summary: Allegations first raised in requests for further review, and late approvals not noted in the complaints, were not reviewed.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review any allegations made for the first time in the requests for further review.

remedy: All members of the Board must attend, in person, the Open Meeting Law training the AG's office conducts in Southborough on November 20, 2019, at 5:30PM at the Southborough Senior Center.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law is ordered for the Board.
